criterion.ownedTruth: Every claim has the standing, evidence and uncertainty it earns.
passConditions: Facts, public statements, bounded inferences and gaps are visibly distinct.
Every evidenced notice resolves to the frozen input and every inference uses at least two sources.
Weak evidence produces abstention while richer evidence earns specificity without false certainty.
The strongest material countercase remains visible in the decision frame or unknowns.
failConditions: A factual, causal or personal claim exceeds its evidence.
A declared strategy or management statement is treated as an observed outcome.
Missing information is filled with generic advice.

hardVetoRules.condition: The output fabricates a source, fact, private belief or causal conclusion.
Cold or sparse evidence is presented as a supported route recommendation.

shared.label: Human agency
shared.rule: Humans own purpose, boundaries, standards, exceptions and the final consequential call.

shared.label: Evidence standing
shared.rule: Keep explicit facts, inferred candidates and behavioural feedback as different data types.

shared.label: Subject and audience boundary
shared.rule: Prove subject, ownership, audience and authority before an item can travel or act.

shared.label: Behavioural reality
shared.rule: Judge the real task and consequence, not an elegant description of the intended system.

optional.label: Claim decomposition
optional.rule: Type the claim, identify its load-bearing assumption and name evidence that would disconfirm it.

optional.label: Strongest countercase
optional.rule: Build the strongest plausible countercase before accepting a confident synthesis.

optional.label: Reversibility and premortem
optional.rule: Test reversibility, premortem failure and opportunity cost separately from predicted upside.

optional.label: Decision quality
optional.rule: Assess the quality of the decision process separately from the eventual outcome.
